scope: Read-only verification of all nine committed-shape diagnostics against local ZIP totals, current crosswalk, listings and final shipping policy; taxonomic labels are supported by source/API evidence. This artifact makes no change to the gate, scorer, overrides, crosswalk or production data.
ninth_row_explanation: Primary 3RNXW=2 plus alias CDG4C=35 gives 37 unique-key records, versus Backbone primary 2765922=2, ratio 18.5. Old COL download 0024806 queried 3RNXW but not CDG4C, so it contained only the primary 2 records for this crosswalk. New download 0026614 queries both spellings. The corrected report now detects the >10x difference, explaining the ninth row. The diagnostic Backbone baseline is not alias-expanded, so this ratio compares the crosswalk primary Backbone key with alias-expanded COL coverage.

taxonomic_review.taxonomy_finding: Backbone v1 has HIGHERRANK with several exact homonymous alternatives, while COL chooses accepted Bartramia stricta Brid. This supplies a new usable match for the literal historical CAN-SAR name. COSEWIC 2023 revised the Canadian Rigid Apple Moss concept to Bartramia aprica after a split of historical stricta; it also records continuing differentiation within the North American aprica concept. Literal-name matching does not establish the current Canadian concept.
taxonomic_review.count_finding: The blank Backbone key was never queried, so zero is a missing baseline match, not evidence that Canadian Rigid Apple Moss had zero occurrences. The COL key contains 13 qualifying records. Biological identity of those 13 records is not established by this aggregate download.
taxonomic_review.open_issue: Current Canadian concept versus historical literal input name; disclose as ambiguity rather than declaring the match biologically correct.

taxonomic_review.taxonomy_finding: Carim et al. 2023 recommend merging richardsoni with the earlier ayresii name. Carim et al. 2024 formally name the western genus Occidentis and retain richardsoni as a junior synonym of ayresii. Supported lump plus genus move under COL26.6 XR, not a simple genus rename or new match.
taxonomic_review.api_relation: EXACT match to synonym 6NVMG Lampetra richardsoni, accepted species KVYB5 Occidentis ayresii. Lampetra ayresii 3S39T also resolves to KVYB5. Pinned COL record calls richardsoni a junior subjective synonym.
taxonomic_review.count_finding: Unproven. A broader accepted species makes aggregation plausible, but taxonomy alone cannot establish the mechanism or magnitude of the 1 to 56 increase. Occurrence identities and original identifications have not been compared.
taxonomic_review.ambiguity: The category is supported for the selected COL treatment. Taxonomic authorities differ, e.g. live ITIS TSN159707 still treats richardsoni as valid; the classification is not a claim of universal consensus.

ITIS separately confirms gentilis laingi is an invalid subsequent combination and atricapillus laingi the valid subspecies. Supported species split plus genus move. The crosswalk additionally aggregates the listing subspecies to its accepted parent species.

taxonomic_review.count_finding: Unproven. A species split and a subsequent genus move do not establish why Canadian totals increased by 33.6x. The pools are accepted species aggregates, not laingi-specific records. Independent occurrence interpretation or download-membership differences need investigation to explain the magnitude.
taxonomic_review.ambiguity: The listing name is subspecies-specific while both diagnostic totals are species-level aggregates. The roll-up is a data-query choice, distinct from taxonomic split/genus changes.

taxonomic_review.taxonomy_finding: McCune and Stone 2022 reduce the three recognized aquatic Peltigera clades to varieties within hydrothyria, including var. gowardii, preserving clade information below species rank. Species Fungorum currently lists both gowardii and its varietal combination as synonyms of hydrothyria. Supported species-level lump/rank reduction, no genus change.
taxonomic_review.api_relation: EXACT match to synonym 76F9M Peltigera gowardii, accepted species 76F7Q Peltigera hydrothyria. The later combination Peltigera hydrothyria var. gowardii CCJYX is also a synonym of 76F7Q in COL26.6 XR.
taxonomic_review.count_finding: Unproven. The lump broadens the accepted species pool, but a 13.1x count gain is not demonstrated to arise solely from that treatment. The original identifications, old hydrothyria records, and occurrence membership have not been audited.
taxonomic_review.ambiguity: Earlier primary work and the 2013 COSEWIC report distinguish western gowardii from eastern hydrothyria. The 2022 paper provides a later alternative rank treatment, and COL uses its broader species concept. COL synonym status does not preserve the accepted variety separately.

independent_taxonomy_review.api_relation: EXACT match to synonym 76F9M Peltigera gowardii, accepted species 76F7Q Peltigera hydrothyria. The later combination Peltigera hydrothyria var. gowardii CCJYX is also a synonym of 76F7Q in COL26.6 XR.

review.scope: Independent read-only classification of three taxonomic name crosswalks. No record-level causation study and no checkout writes.

cases.api_relation: EXACT match to synonym 6NVMG Lampetra richardsoni, accepted species KVYB5 Occidentis ayresii. Lampetra ayresii 3S39T also resolves to KVYB5. Pinned COL record calls richardsoni a junior subjective synonym.
cases.biological_taxonomy: Carim et al. 2023 recommend merging richardsoni with the earlier ayresii name. Carim et al. 2024 formally name the western genus Occidentis and retain richardsoni as a junior synonym of ayresii. Supported lump plus genus move under COL26.6 XR, not a simple genus rename or new match.
cases.count_causation: Unproven. A broader accepted species makes aggregation plausible, but taxonomy alone cannot establish the mechanism or magnitude of the 1 to 56 increase. Occurrence identities and original identifications have not been compared.
cases.ambiguity: The category is supported for the selected COL treatment. Taxonomic authorities differ, e.g. live ITIS TSN159707 still treats richardsoni as valid; the classification is not a claim of universal consensus.

cases.api_relation: EXACT match to synonym 76F9M Peltigera gowardii, accepted species 76F7Q Peltigera hydrothyria. The later combination Peltigera hydrothyria var. gowardii CCJYX is also a synonym of 76F7Q in COL26.6 XR.
cases.biological_taxonomy: McCune and Stone 2022 reduce the three recognized aquatic Peltigera clades to varieties within hydrothyria, including var. gowardii, preserving clade information below species rank. Species Fungorum currently lists both gowardii and its varietal combination as synonyms of hydrothyria. Supported species-level lump/rank reduction, no genus change.
cases.count_causation: Unproven. The lump broadens the accepted species pool, but a 13.1x count gain is not demonstrated to arise solely from that treatment. The original identifications, old hydrothyria records, and occurrence membership have not been audited.
cases.ambiguity: Earlier primary work and the 2013 COSEWIC report distinguish western gowardii from eastern hydrothyria. The 2022 paper provides a later alternative rank treatment, and COL uses its broader species concept. COL synonym status does not preserve the accepted variety separately.

cases.api_relation: EXACT match to subspecies synonym 5FCT5 Accipiter gentilis laingi, accepted subspecies CTQ6K Astur atricapillus laingi, parent species CTQ6J Astur atricapillus. Accipiter gentilis species name 93V5 instead resolves to CVW3C Astur gentilis.
cases.biological_taxonomy: The AOS 2023 supplement separates American atricapillus from Eurasian gentilis. The AOS 2025 supplement transfers both species from Accipiter to Astur. ITIS separately confirms gentilis laingi is an invalid subsequent combination and atricapillus laingi the valid subspecies. Supported species split plus genus move. The crosswalk additionally aggregates the listing subspecies to its accepted parent species.
cases.count_causation: Unproven. A species split and a subsequent genus move do not establish why Canadian totals increased by 33.6x. The pools are accepted species aggregates, not laingi-specific records. Independent occurrence interpretation or download-membership differences need investigation to explain the magnitude.
cases.ambiguity: The listing name is subspecies-specific while both diagnostic totals are species-level aggregates. The roll-up is a data-query choice, distinct from taxonomic split/genus changes.

claim_audit.depth: Taxon-record chains prove the selected checklist relations. Primary taxonomic acts independently support the lump/split/genus labels. A count-difference mechanism was not derived, so no causation claim is made.
claim_audit.breadth: Coverage is exactly these three mappings, not every changed crosswalk. Changes outside these records and record-level reassignments remain untested.
claim_audit.objectivity: Taxonomic concepts depend on the chosen authority and release. COL26.6 XR is explicit; alternative historical and current treatments are stated where relevant. Species roll-up is distinguished from biology.
claim_audit.monoculture: Checked matching API output against pinned ChecklistBank source usages and independently against original taxonomic papers or ITIS/Species Fungorum curated records. These verify taxonomy by different evidence, not multiple re-prompts.

review.conclusion: All three have supported taxonomic classifications and exact API relations; none is classified as a wrong/new match on these records. No taxonomic label proves the observed count-ratio magnitude or listing-specific conservation eligibility.

limitations: Taxonomic relation evidence establishes selected checklist name/concept relations, not the cause or magnitude of an occurrence-count ratio.
Blank Backbone keys are missing queried baselines; zeros for those rows do not prove taxon absence from the Backbone or from Canada.
Diagnostic totals cover species keys before production dropping and range clipping. Production listing counts are supplied separately.
The Backbone baseline uses the crosswalk primary Backbone key; COL totals sum unique primary and alias keys. Redroot therefore exposes asymmetric orthographic coverage.
Backbone and COL downloads were created at different times and use different classification fields; the matched occurrence identities were not compared.
Bartramia stricta is a historical Canadian input name whose current Rigid Apple Moss concept was revised to Bartramia aprica; literal matching remains a biological identity ambiguity.
